output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error in the cooperative's own systems, not to the fungicide, Lower Serra growers, or Meridane. The mandarin product record in the new documentation suite was copied from the avocado record on 1 Aug, and its carriage temperature stayed at 7.0°C. The spec for mandarins is 4.0°C. All five Meridane containers sent through that system ran at 7°C and were rejected. Every container set at 4°C passed, including those packed with the new fungicide, and the Coastway containers passed too. The carrier's logs and your own loggers show the units held the setpoint they were given, so a claim against Meridane would fail. Suspending Lower Serra growers and withholding their pay is not supported. Their fruit made up 28–40% of every container, accepted ones included. The pallet survey covered only rejected containers, so it can't show that their fruit was worse. Reverting the fungicide isn't supported either. What to do now: correct the record to 4.0°C. One container is at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and one is queued for 10 Oct, so have Meridane reset both to 4.0°C right away. Add a pre-submission check of reefer settings against the product spec, and review how the 3 Aug sign-off missed this. Hold off on the claim, the suspension and the invoice deduction. I'm quite sure of this. The remaining uncertainty is whether Lower Serra fruit is more vulnerable at higher temperatures.
